title: Change a Tire
summary: Flat on the shoulder? Jay always said: secure the car first, then swap the wheel.

learn.heading: What you're looking at
learn.body: A flat tire means the car is riding on rubber that can't hold air. You'll find the spare (usually under the trunk floor or mounted under the rear), a jack, and a lug wrench in the trunk. The lug nuts hold the wheel to the hub. The jack goes on a solid frame point — never on plastic trim.

learn.heading: What can hurt you
learn.body: A car that rolls off a jack can crush you. Never crawl fully under a car supported only by a jack. Work on level ground, set the parking brake, and block the wheel diagonally opposite the flat. If you're on a road shoulder, turn on hazards and stay aware of traffic.
learn.callout: Jack stands are for real work under a car. A roadside spare change is jack-only — keep your body out from under the vehicle.

learn.heading: The steps
learn.body:
1. Park safely, hazards on, parking brake set.
2. Block the opposite wheel with a rock, brick, or wedge.
3. Loosen lug nuts a quarter turn each while the tire still touches the ground.
4. Place the jack on the correct lift point and raise until the flat clears the ground.
5. Remove lug nuts, pull the wheel off, mount the spare, hand-tighten nuts in a star pattern.
6. Lower until the tire touches ground, tighten nuts fully in a star pattern, then lower jack completely.
7. Stow the flat and tools. Drive to get the flat repaired — spares are temporary.

practice.prompt: Tap the parts you need before you lift the car.
practice.failMessage: You need the jack, lug wrench, and spare before you lift. Everything else can wait.

practice.prompt: Put the tire change steps in the right order.

steps.text: Block the wheel opposite the flat
Loosen lug nuts while tire is on the ground
Jack up the car at the frame point
Remove flat, mount spare, hand-tighten lug nuts
Lower car and fully tighten lug nuts in a star pattern

practice.failMessage: Loosen nuts on the ground first. Jack only after the car is secured and nuts are cracked loose.

practice.prompt: Spot what's dangerous in this roadside setup.

hazards.label: Jack on soft dirt at an angle
Spare tire laid out and ready

practice.failMessage: No parking brake and a jack on soft ground — that's how a car rolls off the jack.
